statistic: Monroe County has 2,291 licensed psychologists, clinical social workers, mental health counselors and marriage and family therapists: 423 psychologists, 990 LCSWs, 734 LMHCs and 144 LMFTs, counted by mailing address as of July 1, 2026.
source: NYSED Office of the Professions, license statistics

statistic: That is 305.3 clinicians per 100,000 residents, against 285.9 statewide and 193.4 in the five neighboring counties (Genesee, Livingston, Ontario, Orleans and Wayne).
source: NYSED license statistics; U.S. Census Bureau 2025 population estimates

statistic: Monroe ranks 13th of New York's 62 counties for these clinicians per resident, and 8th for psychologists (56.4 per 100,000).
Monroe has 144 licensed marriage and family therapists, 9.5% of New York's 1,518 and the second-highest count of any county after Manhattan.
source: NYSED license statistics, marriage and family therapists

statistic: New York issued 5,611 new licenses in these four professions in 2025, up 25% from 4,485 in 2024.
source: NYSED license statistics, licenses issued by year

statistic: The federal government designates a mental health professional shortage area for Medicaid-eligible residents of 88 census tracts, most of them in the City of Rochester (HRSA's name for it is "ME-City of Rochester"): 129,319 people, with a shortage score of 19 (higher scores mean greater need). The designation dates from June 28, 2022.
geography: Rochester area: 88 census tracts, mostly in the City of Rochester (Medicaid-eligible population)
source: HRSA, Health Professional Shortage Areas (mental health), designation "ME-City of Rochester"

statistic: An estimated 32.5% of Monroe County adults feel lonely always, usually or sometimes, close to the median for New York's 62 counties (32.3%).

In the City of Rochester the estimate is 37.2%, against 28.3% to 32.6% in 18 of the county's 20 suburban towns. 23 of the 25 census tracts where 40% or more of adults are estimated to be lonely are in the city.
source: CDC PLACES 2025 release, place and census tract estimates

statistic: An estimated 22.9% of Monroe County adults lack the social and emotional support they need; in the City of Rochester, 28.7%.

An estimated 15.3% of Monroe County adults have frequent mental distress (14 or more poor mental health days in the past month), below the median for New York's 62 counties (16.2%); in the City of Rochester, 18.8%.
An estimated 21.9% of Monroe County adults have ever been told they have depression, tied with two other counties for the 6th highest share among New York's 62 counties.
Monroe County residents had 7,151 babies in 2023, down 18% from 8,707 in 2008.
source: NYS Department of Health, Vital Statistics of New York State 2023, Table 7

statistic: In 2022, 12.4% of mothers in New York State outside New York City reported symptoms of postpartum depression after giving birth (11.9% statewide).
geography: New York State excluding New York City
source: NYS Department of Health, from CDC PRAMS 2022 survey data

statistic: Applied to Monroe County births, that rate suggests about 890 mothers a year are likely to report symptoms of postpartum depression. This is an estimate, not a count.
unit: mothers a year likely to report symptoms (estimate)
source: Ruzicka Psychology calculation from NYS DOH Table 7 and PRAMS

statistic: 82.4% of New York mothers who had a postpartum checkup were asked about depression in 2020, up from 76.1% in 2016.
source: NYS Department of Health, from New York PRAMS data

statistic: 3,008 couples married in Monroe County in 2023, and county courts granted 1,387 divorces.
source: NYS Department of Health, Vital Statistics of New York State 2023, Tables 47 and 48

statistic: 39% of those divorces involved at least one child under 18, and 59% ended a marriage of 10 years or more.
source: NYS Department of Health, Vital Statistics 2023, Tables 51 and 52

statistic: In October 2026, 44,679 calls to 988 were routed to New York's crisis centers, and 91% (40,544) were answered in state. 847 went to the national backup network. These are statewide figures; the report does not break them down by county.
unit: of routed calls answered in state
source: 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline, In-State KPI Report, October 2026

statistic: Calls answered in New York were picked up in an average of 30.9 seconds.
source: 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline, In-State KPI Report, October 2026
